raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

A single request with `structured_outputs={"json_object": false}` or `{"json": ""}` crashes the **EngineCore** process: the request returns 500 `EngineDeadError` and every subsequent request fails (instance-wide DoS).

`StructuredOutputsParams` counts constraints with `is not None`, so `json_object=False` (`False is not None`) and `json=""` (`"" is not None`) are treated as "a constraint is set" → a `StructuredOutputRequest` is built and sent to the engine. But `get_structured_output_key()` only returns `JSON_OBJECT` when `json_object` is truthy, so `False` falls through to `raise ValueError("No valid structured output parameter found")`; an empty `json` schema fails in the xgrammar compiler. These `ValueError`s are raised inside the EngineCore step loop, which has no per-request isolation, so one bad request kills the engine.

Fix: reject both inputs during request validation in `SamplingParams._validate_structured_outputs` (called by `verify()`, frontend → 400), next to the existing empty-grammar / empty-choice guards:
- `json` is an empty string → `ValueError` (mirrors the empty-grammar guard).
- `json_object is False` → `ValueError` (`json_object` is a flag; only `True` selects a constraint; omit `structured_outputs` to disable).

The bad request now fails fast at the frontend and the engine keeps serving. The deeper per-request engine-step exception isolation is a separate, larger change and is intentionally out of scope here.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `tests/v1/structured_output/test_utils.py` exercises `_validate_structured_outputs` for both inputs (CPU).
- E2E: real `vllm serve`, send a degenerate request then a normal request, and check engine survival.

## Test Result

E2E (real `vllm serve`), one bad request followed by a normal request:

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `structured_outputs={"json_object": false}` | 500 `EngineDeadError` | 400 `BadRequestError` |
| follow-up normal request | connection refused (engine dead) | 200, normal generation |
| `structured_outputs={"json": ""}` | engine crash | 400 `BadRequestError` |
| follow-up normal request | n/a (engine dead) | 200, normal generation |

Unit tests: with fix `2 passed`; revert the fix and both FAIL (neither input raises). Full `pre-commit run --files` passed (ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy, SPDX, and all vLLM custom hooks).

<details>
<summary>E2E repro (env + serve + client + observed output)</summary>

Environment:
- GPU: NVIDIA A800-80GB (sm80)
- vLLM: `main`
- Model: `google/gemma-3-1b-it` (substitute; the failure is in request validation / the structured-output path and is model-agnostic, so any small model reproduces it)

Serve:

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-3-1b-it --served-model-name m \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 1024 --port 8000
```

Trigger + survival probe:

```bash
# 1) degenerate request
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"m","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8,"structured_outputs":{"json_object":false}}' \
  -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n'

# 2) normal request, to check the engine is still alive
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"m","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n'
```

Before the fix:
- request (1): `HTTP=500 {"type":"InternalServerError"}`; server log: `ValueError: No valid structured output parameter found` → `EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue`.
- request (2): connection refused (`HTTP=000`); the EngineCore process is dead, so every later request fails.
- `structured_outputs={"json":""}` behaves the same (engine crash inside the xgrammar compiler).

After the fix:
- request (1): `HTTP=400 {"message":"structured_outputs.json_object must be True if set; omit structured_outputs to disable structured outputs","type":"BadRequestError"}`.
- request (2): `HTTP=200`, normal generation; the engine stays alive.
- `structured_outputs={"json":""}`: `HTTP=400 {"message":"structured_outputs.json cannot be an empty string"}`, engine stays alive.
- Server log shows only the frontend `ValueError`, no `EngineCore failed` / `EngineDeadError`.

</details>

AI assistance was used to investigate, reproduce, and draft this change; the author reviewed the diff and validation output.

Thanks @vadiklyutiy. Merged latest main and updated the test for the new `_validate_structured_outputs(model_config, ...)` signature from #45436.

I moved the degenerate-rejection test out of `test_utils.py` (which covers `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features`) into `test_validation.py`, next to the other `_validate_structured_outputs` tests. It reuses the existing `_StubModelConfig` helper and inherits that file's `cpu_test` marker, so it runs in the `v1/structured_output` cpu job (`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`). That same `pytest -v -s v1/structured_output` glob also collects `test_utils.py`. I verified the new test passes against main and fails when the fix is reverted.
Sibling degenerate inputs `regex=""` and `structural_tag=""` follow the same "is not None counts it, truthiness skips it" pattern and aren't guarded. Would be good to fix in follow up review.

Hi @vadiklyutiy. Checked both on latest `main`; neither crashes the engine: - `regex=""` compiles to a grammar matching only the empty string, so it returns 200 (empty output) with the engine alive. - `structural_tag=""` is already rejected with 400 at the frontend (`protocol.py`), so it never reaches the engine. So not the same DoS class as `json=""`. Guarding `regex=""` would turn a currently-valid request into a 400; happy to add symmetric validation in a follow-up if you'd prefer the consistency. E2E (real vllm serve, Qwen3-0.6B) | `structured_outputs` | HTTP | engine | |---|---|---| | `{"regex": ""}` | 200, empty output | alive | | `{"structural_tag": ""}` | 400 (frontend) | alive |

@Sunt-ing, please sync your PR with main again please.
Test [buildkite/ci/pr/async-engine-inputs-utils-worker-config-cpu](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/75128#019f13cb-d2a7-4e13-a93e-8445878d2595) was reported as broken [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47068) and then fixed in this [PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47015).
As far as I see, `self.structured_outputs.json` object could also be a dict. What would be if someone passed json as empty dict? Should we in this case reject this schema as well or not?

nodes.body:
Hi @arpera, I checked on a live server: an empty dict is fine and should not be rejected. `json={}` is the canonical "any JSON value" schema. `get_structured_output_key` serializes it with `json.dumps({})` to `"{}"`, which xgrammar compiles to a permissive grammar, so the request returns 200 and the engine stays alive. The crash is specific to the empty *string*: `json.loads("")` raises `JSONDecodeError` inside the xgrammar compiler, which runs in the engine step loop with no per-request isolation. So `{}` is a valid (if unusual) request, and rejecting it would be a regression; this guard intentionally targets only the empty string.
E2E on real vllm serve (Qwen3-0.6B), one request each followed by a survival probe | `structured_outputs` | HTTP | engine after | |---|---|---| | `{"json": {}}` | 200, generates a valid JSON value | alive (200) | | `{"json": {"type": "object"}}` | 200, valid JSON object | alive (200) | | `{"json": ""}` | 500 `EngineDeadError` | dead (next request: connection refused) |

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+        (StructuredOutputsParams(json=""), "json cannot be an empty string"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_degenerate_structured_outputs_rejected(structured_outputs, match):
+    """json_object=False and an empty json schema pass the `is not None`

             and self.structured_outputs.grammar.strip() == ""
         ):
